anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Its approved L1 configuration presents a small fixed 5x5x3 voxel pile with four targets, one hazard, one support constraint, and simplified rotate controls. The agent must still coordinate camera rotation, raycast selection, mining durability, and support preservation. Letter Rapids d1 has broad probability bands, a visible phrase, no occlusion or support topology, and a direct next-symbol action; its d1 profile is plausibly no harder than this L1 anchor.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 full configuration requires sustained analog tilt with acceleration, friction, bounce, walls, hazards, and ordered lamps before reaching the goal. Letter Rapids d4 full also requires continuous pointer control and ticked feedback, but exposes the target phrase and the next letter's visible band, has no route search or physical obstacles, and uses rewind for local recovery. Its motor timing and context-dependent reflow support a level above the L3 anchor, while its planning burden is lower.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 simplified configuration searches a changing 5x5 board for a bounded exact-score route across multi-wave cascades and refills, while avoiding forbidden candy. Letter Rapids d5 has longer phrases and stricter continuous control, but the target sequence is explicit, each next symbol is locally visible, and there is no branching score/search problem. The Letter Rapids ladder is therefore below this L5 planning anchor even though its full mode can be more motor-demanding.

visible_baseline_solution: The screenshot-only full-mode solution reads the target phrase shown in the header, identifies the next required character in the currently rendered probability-sized canyon band, moves the pointer vertically into that band, and holds horizontal position to the right of the forward edge to advance. It returns to the dead zone to brake or hold, and moves left of the reverse edge to rewind a wrong committed character. After each commit the visible row is reweighted using the new output context, so the agent re-aims from the new screen. Success is the exact target output with a terminal target state; excess rewinds or travel terminate unsuccessfully. The phrase is visible, so this is sequential visual control and re-aiming rather than hidden-string recall or language inference.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The d4/full baseline is materially more demanding than the L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board in local motor precision and state-dependent row reflow, while it remains below the L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade in branching planning and hidden consequence management. It is also much harder than the L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine profile's small, simplified, mostly discrete interaction. The d4 bundle is coherent: a 27-symbol alphabet including space, rare six-character targets, narrow control zones, high current amplitude, and only two rewinds, with the next required symbol always recoverable from the visible screen.

findings.claim: The d4-to-d5 minimum-band parameter is not a strong visible distinction because both source rows are redistributed through a fixed 340 display-band floor.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator supplies minimum_band_milli values of 110 for d4 and 70 for d5, but the browser and grader first apply display_band_floor_milli=340 and redistribute the row. With the same 27-symbol alphabet, the minimum-floor change affects only the residual free-width allocation; it is likely to be a subpixel-scale difference on the displayed canvas. D4 and d5 remain distinguishable through longer target phrases, higher current/speed/jitter, and the narrower dead zone, so this finding weakens one claimed step rather than collapsing the profiles.

evidence.explanation: D4 minimum_band_milli is 110 and d5 is 70 while the alphabet remains the same.
The generated simulation carries a shared display_band_floor_milli of 340 for all profiles.
The visible row applies the 340 floor and redistributes the source probabilities before rendering.
The authoritative replay uses the same fixed-floor display-row transformation.

findings.recommended_action: Measure the rendered d4 and d5 band widths in an isolated headless screenshot if minimum-band visibility is intended as a difficulty lever. If it is not perceptually meaningful, revise that parameter or document the d4-to-d5 distinction as coming from target length and control dynamics rather than band width.

concise_summary: Keep Letter Rapids at the current d4/full baseline. The source supports a coherent ordered d1-d5 ladder and interaction-equivalent simplified/full pairs: d4 is above the L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board in precision and state-dependent reflow but below the L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade in branching planning. The d4-to-d5 minimum-band change is weak because of the shared display floor, but other d5 changes preserve a distinguishable harder profile.
